channel.title: Bearings
channel.description: A weekly audio digest on care, chaplaincy and leadership, with deep dives on request. Made for one listener.
channel.itunes:author: Bearings
channel.itunes:summary: A weekly audio digest on care, chaplaincy and leadership, with deep dives on request.

item.title: Deep dive – The care home that became a software company
item.description: Bira Care Homes, a seven-home family group in South Wales and Herefordshire, is selling the AI care management system it built for itself, with a claim of up to seventy per cent less administration that nobody outside the firm has checked: who builds care software, what independent evidence says about time saved, and a rulebook that approves no product and leaves safety to the buyer. Then where a chaplain's work sits in the record, what the impact framework should measure first, home-made tools and AI and Our Values, and the three decisions a chief executive would make.

item.title: Deep dive – A seat nobody filled
item.description: Wales made a seat for care workers on its seven regional partnership boards law in December 2024, and Unison says none has filled it: the consultation in which all seven boards opposed the seat, the duty that arrived with no role description or nomination route, boards with no legal self, the thin evidence on worker voice, and a new government that wants to put the boards on a statutory footing. Then the four ways a written commitment fails, run against Chaplain Working Agreements and the rest of Phase One, and what a chief executive would check before fair pay bargaining arrives in 2028.

item.title: Deep dive – Care as the first job
item.description: Alan Milburn's review of the million young people out of work and learning: the Youth Opportunity Service, the two guarantees, the bargain with employers and the benefit changes that pay for it, the arguments against, and the four paragraphs asking social care to take on more young people when the King's Fund finds over half of under-twenties leave within a year. Then what civic service and the first year in care mean for chaplains and Walking Together, and how a chief executive would fix the welcome before widening the door.

item.title: Deep dive – Faith, spirituality and a better later life
item.description: The Padua meta-analysis in PLOS Aging and Health behind last week's headline: 21 studies and 5,664 older people, a moderate link between faith and quality of life that is weakest in Europe, drawn from snapshots of people mostly living at home in far more religious countries, with nothing on care homes, Britain or chaplaincy itself. Then how to use it for Walking Together – identity, the skills framework, the rhythm of chaplaincy and an impact framework that fills the gap – and the line a chief executive would draw on what MHA can claim.

item.title: Deep dive – The first national guidance on AI in social care
item.description: The joint government guidance of 20 November: four principles that keep the decision with the practitioner, where it came from, and what the evidence from the London School of Economics, the Ada Lovelace Institute, SCIE and Care England says about bias, oversight and where the saved time goes. Then what it means for AI and Our Values, chaplains' records and funeral tributes, and Walking Together, and the test a chief executive would apply.

item.title: Bearings No. 4 – Nothing unchecked
item.description: The first national guidance on AI in social care, the Methodist Church's apology after a former President's conviction, and new evidence linking spirituality to a better later life. Then seven more in brief, and this week's leadership question: what does your team know that you don't?

item.title: Deep dive – Fix the ordinary work before you add AI
item.description: The Housing LIN's AI survey of specialist and supported housing, and four responses to it: only eight of 33 providers had evaluated their AI and five of 40 had involved residents, while two small providers cut empty-room time from fifteen days to five by sorting out their process first. Then the new government and CQC expectations, what it means for AI and Our Values and Walking Together, and what a chief executive would check before the 31 January telecare switch-off.

item.title: Deep dive – Who is in charge of social care?
item.description: The Nuffield Trust and Institute for Government's governance report for the Casey Commission: how England's care system came to have no steward, the choices on eligibility, fees, market oversight and workforce, and what nine other countries do. Then what it means for MHA and Walking Together, and how a chief executive would prepare before the Commission reports in summer 2027.

item.title: Bearings No. 3 – No one is in charge
item.description: Casey's first evidence on who runs social care, a Jewish care home that lets researchers move in, and the housing roadmap for later life. Then six more in brief, and this week's leadership question: what problem does your strategy solve?
